current_date: Adopted 25 February 2026 (stated in the document's Introduction); takes effect 1 June 2026 (council page)
current_evidence: The council's 'Make a planning application' page (updated 2 September 2026) links this 'Planning Application Validation List' PDF as adopted 25 February 2026 and taking effect 1 June 2026, consistent with the Feb 2026 Planning Policy Committee report 'Planning Application Validation Requirements 2026-2028'.

issues.detail: The list date 2026-08-01 comes from PDF CreationDate metadata. The document itself says it was adopted on 25 February 2026, and the council page says it took effect on 1 June 2026. The PDF cites SPA guidance 'adopted ... June 2026', so the file was probably re-saved after adoption. Even so, the list date should be the adoption date, 2026-02-25.
issues.evidence: Introduction: 'This document was adopted on 25 February 2026 following consultation.'

issues.detail: Householder is recorded as '(none)', but section 5 has a local table. It lists: CIL Form 1 and 2. Daylight/Sunlight Plan, a 1:100 or 1:200 site plan with a 45-degree line (60 degrees for single-storey extensions in the former Daventry District) where extensions adjoin residential properties, plus a full assessment if the line is breached. Dropped Kerb Plan, for providing or altering a vehicular access. Ecology Preliminary Roost Assessment, where a vacant building is converted or demolished or has potential roost features. Flood Risk Assessment, for householder and minor extensions up to 250 sqm in Flood Zones 2 and 3, setting out floor levels or flood-proofing. External Wall Insulation details, for householder EWI applications. Parking Plan, for extra bedrooms or changes affecting parking spaces or driveways. Tree protection plan, where trees are within or next to the site.
issues.evidence: Section 5 Householder Applications, Local Requirement table (pp.18-21)

issues.detail: Grokbot never captured these local requirements from the Major (s8), Minor residential (s9) and Minor commercial (s10) tables under any application type. Air Quality Assessment: development likely to cause pollution or expose occupiers to it. Health Impact Assessment: majors. Sustainability Statement: all four full/outline tables. Housing Quality Statement: residential, to NDSS standards (only fragments appear, as 'Housing mix' and 'Sunlight to gardens'). Landscape and Visual Impact Assessment: where the LPA considers visual or landscape impacts notable. Play and Open Space Statement: majors. Parking and access arrangement plan. Swept Path plan: majors, refuse vehicle tracking at 1:500 or 1:1000. Phasing Plan: large-scale majors with phasing. Site Layout Plan: majors. Schedule of development: new dwellings or residential/commercial floorspace. Schedule of plans/drawings: new dwellings or change of use. Public Transport Strategy: development generating notable demand for sustainable modes. Site Photos: all applications, plus contextual elevations and 3D visualisations for all majors. Rural Enterprise Statement: rural worker's dwelling. Independent Design Review Panel report: NPPF para 84(e) homes. The retail and main town centre Sequential Test was captured but mislabelled as a flood test.
issues.evidence: s8 Local Requirement: 'Air Quality Assessment', 'Health Impact Assessment', 'Sustainability Statement', 'Plan: Swept Path'; s9: 'Rural Enterprise Statement for creation of a rural worker's dwelling'

issues.detail: Listed building consent is recorded as '(none)', but section 7 has a local table. It lists: Ecology Preliminary Roost Assessment. Fabric condition survey, where historic features are to be renewed or replaced on grounds of poor condition. Heritage Statement. Method Statement for the repair and alteration works. Existing and proposed elevations, floor plans, roof plans and sections. Specific plans at no less than 1:20 for architectural details such as doors, windows, shopfronts and mouldings. Site photographs. Structural Report, for major alteration or demolition, structural repairs, or conversions.

issues.detail: Prior approvals have no correct local requirements in Grokbot. Its only row is a misfiled Sequential Test. Section 15 (Prior Approval under Permitted Development) requires: CIL Form 1 and 2. Biodiversity Checklist with a PEAR. Rural Building Questionnaire, for agricultural prior approvals. SAMM payment, for a net increase in dwellings within the Upper Nene Valley Gravel Pits SPA buffer. Site photos. Technical information where constraints or consultees raise concern: transport statement, FRA, land contamination, noise, odour, air quality, site waste management plan and archaeological DBA. Section 16 (prior approval for larger extensions and additional storeys) requires CIL forms, existing and proposed floor plans, elevations and roof plans, and proposed sections for additional storeys.
issues.evidence: s15 Local Requirement: 'Rural Building Questionnaire For Agricultural Prior Approval'; 'Technical Information for Prior Approval Application'

issues.detail: Variation of condition (s73) and Non-material amendment are both '(none)', but sections 19 and 11 have local tables. Both list: Drawing Schedule, for majors. Marketing Report, where removing an occupancy or restrictive-use condition. Overlay existing and proposed elevations, floor plans and roof plans. Planning Statement explaining the change (for NMAs, why it is non-material). Updated plans and documents for majors (phasing plan, drawing schedule, housing statement; for s73 also ecology reports). Viability Appraisal with an updated planning obligations statement, where affordable housing or contributions fall below policy. Section 19 also requires CIL Forms 1 and 2.
issues.evidence: s19 Local Requirement: 'Marketing Report where the application concerns the removal of an occupancy or restrictive use condition'

issues.detail: Four key rows take their trigger from a neighbouring row. Flood Risk Assessment uses the bat Preliminary Roost Assessment text; the real trigger is Flood Zone 2/3, over 1 ha in Flood Zone 1, a change to a more vulnerable use, within 10 m of a watercourse, next to a flood defence, or raising land levels. Drainage Strategy uses daylight text; the real trigger is all majors, minor residential of 5-9 dwellings, or minors creating or changing use of 500-999 sqm. Waste/Refuse uses Sequential Test text; the Site Waste Management Plan applies to all residential development, including changes of use, that affects waste. 'Sequential / Exception Test (flood)' is the retail and main town centre Sequential Test (outside a defined centre; over 2,500 sqm at outline), and its trigger is the 'Schedule of plans/drawing' sentence. The document has no flood sequential or exception test requirement.
issues.evidence: s8: 'Flood Risk Assessment Any development falling into the following categories: - within flood zone 2 or 3...'; 'Sequential Test Any proposals for retail and other Main Town Centre uses...'

issues.detail: Other rows use text from the wrong requirement. BNG uses the discharge-of-conditions heading; the local BNG requirement is a habitat condition assessment, draft Biodiversity Gain Plan, draft post-development metric and habitats plan if not exempt. Biodiversity Checklist uses the national Biodiversity Statement text; it should be 'complete the Checklist in Appendix 1 of the Biodiversity SPD'. Crime Statement uses mostly daylight text. Design and Access Statement and Heritage Statement use the demolition-only heritage text. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' uses the Demolition Method Statement. Cycle parking and Highways/access use generic block-plan and location-plan guidance. Photographs uses the Householder EWI item. SCI uses the national wind-turbine row; the local Community Engagement Statement applies to majors, and at outline to large minors and above.
issues.evidence: Grokbot BNG trigger '(England) 2015 BNG condition requires discharging Fee'; s8 'Statement of Community Involvement A Community Engagement Statement is required...'

issues.detail: Several triggers are garbled or run into the next row. CIL merges the CIL, Daylight and Dropped Kerb headings. Daylight/Sunlight merges with the CIL and Dropped Kerb text and loses the 45/60-degree site-plan test. Lighting runs into the LVIA text. Street Scene runs into the Planning Obligations Statement. The Outline Travel Plan includes page-header noise ('45 Information What is required') and was apparently filed under Outline only because the text says 'should outline the way'. The Block plan, floor plan, roof plan and levels rows concatenate several plan rows with Article 7 citations. Odour gives only the minor-commercial extraction trigger; for majors and outline the trigger is residential development in high-odour areas.
issues.evidence: Grokbot CIL trigger: 'Completed CIL Form 1 and 2 National Requirements Daylight/Sunlight Plan/Assessment Dropped Kerb Plan...'

summary: Grokbot links the current West Northamptonshire list, Planning Application Validation Requirements 2026-2028, adopted 25 Feb 2026. Its list date comes from PDF metadata. The extraction is poor. The document has a local table for each of 21 application types, but Grokbot put about 47 requirements under Full planning as INFERRED. It leaves Householder, Reserved matters, LBC, s73, NMA, LDC, adverts, prior approvals and discharge of conditions empty, gives Outline only a Travel Plan, and misses requirements such as Air Quality, Sustainability Statement and Housing Quality Statement. Many triggers come from the wrong row; for example, the FRA uses the bat-roost text and the Drainage Strategy uses the daylight text. The list should be re-extracted section by section.
